purpose: The written criteria every creative review cites. A REJECT must name at least one id from this file (ulac/creative.py refuses one that does not). The standard that explains them is creative_standard.md.

lenses.story: Story editor: what the audience understands, wants, fears and learns, and whether each sequence earns its place.
lenses.craft: Director and cinematographer: staging, framing, lens, height, movement, light, colour, performance and sound.
lenses.audience: Audience advocate for ages 4 to 8: comprehension from the picture, attention, emotional precision and care.

levels.concept: Judged on the creative brief before any storyboard.
levels.sequence: Judged on each sequence's CREATIVE.json before its storyboard is approved.
levels.film: Judged by a person on the assembled cut.

criteria.criterion: Materially different concepts were developed and compared before one was chosen.
criteria.pass: At least three concepts. Every pair differs in at least two of: vantage (whose point of view the camera keeps), time handling, what the picture adds beyond the words, structural device.
criteria.fail: Concepts that differ only in palette, weather, set dressing or shot list; a single concept with variations.
criteria.code: CONCEPTS_TOO_FEW, CONCEPTS_NOT_DISTINCT (counts and compares the four strategy fields; it cannot judge whether the difference matters)

criteria.criterion: The chosen concept's distinction is demonstrated, not asserted.
criteria.pass: At least three named choices that a straightforward adaptation of the same text would not make, each tied to sequence ids and to what it changes for the audience.
criteria.fail: 'Fresh', 'unique', 'cinematic' with no named choice; originality claimed because a concept was newly generated.
criteria.code: DISTINCTION_THIN (counts entries and their sequence ids)

criteria.criterion: Swap test: the key images belong to this story.
criteria.pass: Each key image would lose its meaning if moved into another episode of the series.
criteria.fail: Images that fit any episode: a child smiles at the robot, the robot's lights glow.

criteria.criterion: Text fidelity: the treatment serves the narration and never contradicts it.
criteria.pass: Narration words and order unchanged unless the client approved a change; no image shows what the text says did not happen.
criteria.fail: A device that shows deliberate reasoning where the text says the answer 'just showed up'; a reordered or trimmed line without the client's approval.
criteria.code: none (judgement; narration changes are a producer escalation)

criteria.pass: Every surprise, device or striking image is set up on screen before it pays off and is consistent with the characters and the world.
criteria.fail: Random weirdness; a visual device that appears once and is never explained or paid off.

criteria.pass: Names what the audience understands, feels, anticipates or questions at its end, and that differs from the sequence before.
criteria.fail: Consecutive sequences whose audience answer is the same or interchangeable.
criteria.code: FIELD_MISSING, BOILERPLATE (presence and near-duplicate text only)

criteria.pass: Names who wants what in this sequence and what stands in the way.
criteria.fail: 'The scene continues'; a want with no obstacle across several sequences.

criteria.pass: Knowledge, feeling, relationship, position or power differs between the opening and the closing of the sequence, and the picture shows it.
criteria.fail: A sequence whose closing state equals its opening state, so that only the narration advances.

criteria.pass: Key developments come from a choice a character makes on screen, in a way only that character would make it.
criteria.fail: An outcome that simply happens to the protagonist; a choice any character could have made in the same words.

criteria.pass: Names the specific information, feeling, setup or payoff lost if the sequence were cut or shot generically.
criteria.fail: 'It continues the scene'; the same answer repeated across sequences.

criteria.criterion: The theme is acted before it is said.
criteria.pass: The lesson is dramatized by what characters do before any line states it.
criteria.fail: The theme exists only in the closing narration.

criteria.pass: Names at least one thing the image tells that the narration does not say: a reaction, a consequence, a spatial relation, a scale, a subtext. Literal illustration may accompany it, never replace it.
criteria.fail: EP05 SEQ_010: each sampled frame shows the action the narration names at that moment (sitting on the bed, then an insert of the gesture), and nothing the words do not already say.

criteria.pass: Size, height, vantage and movement are each justified by what the audience must understand or feel at that moment.
criteria.fail: A medium two-shot with a slow push chosen by default (EP05: 17 of 37 plans contain a slow push; 24 of 37 open on a medium or two-shot).
criteria.code: CAMERA_VALUE_UNKNOWN, FIELD_MISSING (enumerated values present; motivation is judgement)

criteria.pass: No setup repeated across more than three consecutive sequences and no move type in more than 40 % of sequences, unless the plan records why (a motif, a deliberate hold).
criteria.fail: EP05 bedroom act: 35 of 66 sampled frames are the same eye-level bedside two-shot.
criteria.code: REPETITION (REVIEW: answered with repetition_reason, or REJECT material)

criteria.criterion: A written visual language exists before rendering.
criteria.pass: The brief sets rules for lens, height, vantage, movement, depth, light, colour, silhouette and blocking, and says how they change as the story changes.
criteria.fail: Style left to the model; rules that never change from the first scene to the last.

criteria.pass: Names the performance (gesture, timing, held beat) that carries the sequence's emotion. MACA performs with visor, lights, posture and hands; she has no mouth.
criteria.fail: Emotion carried only by the narration; generic idle motion.

criteria.pass: Names the sound perspective (whose ears) and at least one dramatic sound decision: a drop-out, a silence, an off-screen sound, a change of distance. Embedded audio stays SFX, foley and ambience only.
criteria.fail: The same ambience bed in every sequence.

criteria.pass: The set, seats, props and identities hold; the camera changes.
criteria.fail: Varying the room instead of the camera (EP05-C05), or keeping one setup to stay consistent.

criteria.pass: At each key beat a viewer aged 4 to 8 can tell from the picture alone who is there, where they are and what just happened.
criteria.fail: A key beat that exists only in words.

criteria.pass: The feeling at each key beat is named precisely (embarrassed, not sad) and shown by a specific action.
criteria.fail: Generic smiles and generic sadness.

criteria.pass: Any single setup held longer than 8 s states what keeps a child watching: a performance change, a reveal, a sound.
criteria.fail: EP05 SEQ_022 and SEQ_027 hold one setup for about 14 s each (all three sampled frames); their plans name a camera move, not what holds a child's attention.

criteria.pass: Embarrassment, fear or unkindness is shown at the intensity the story needs and is resolved on screen; no image models harm without consequence.
criteria.fail: Humiliation played for laughs; frightening imagery the story does not need.

criteria.pass: The plan names designed key images (at least three), each specific to this story and set up so it lands.
criteria.fail: No image a child could describe the next day. EP05's that would pass: SEQ_006c to SEQ_007b, SEQ_028b.

criteria.criterion: A person watches the whole film as an audience member.
criteria.pass: One uninterrupted watch, recorded with the person's name and date: where attention drifted, any confusion, the emotional peak, whether the ending lands. MATERIAL notes are fixed or approved.
criteria.fail: Quality declared from gate results; a watch recorded by an agent.

criteria.pass: Each criterion is recorded pass or fail with its evidence. A failing non-negotiable blocks whatever else passed.
criteria.fail: A total or average that lets a strong area hide a failing one.
